correctness.rationale: The 15 free binary upper-triangular entries give a bijection with exactly 32768 masks. For each mask, the exact finite-field recursive definition E^k=sum_{i=1}^{k-1} E^i E^(k-i) is implemented by bilinear products of span bases and finite GF(2) elimination; an independent coordinate-product and XOR-span-closure implementation verifies every one of the 32768 indices. Classical maximal index 33 gives finite guaranteed cutoff. Re-running the included self-contained checker returns the thirteen counts summing to 32768, explicit witnesses and VERIFY_OK; the 33 bin independently matches the known 5-superdiagonal constraint. The F2 triangularization theorem turns the exhaustive presentation spectrum into the full isomorphism-invariant F2 nilpotent evolution-algebra spectrum. No extrapolation from this finite census to a general infinite-field theorem is made.

value.rationale: The exhaustive n=6 binary spectrum directly tests an explicitly motivated 2026 Conjecture 9 whose n=6 evidence consisted of random trials over a large prime. It supplies a complete, reproducible finite-field cutoff and all thirteen exact natural nilpotency-index probabilities in the uniform labelled strictly triangular model, rather than isolated examples or the already-known maximal index count. The very rare index 10 (64 among 32768) illustrates why random sampling need not robustly detect every stratum. It remains a finite-field test, not a proof of the infinite-field conjecture or an isomorphism-class census.
